description: What success is measured against. Captured at setup and framed into every forecast. Company and personal goals are tracked separately because they often differ — a rep can hit quota in a quarter the company misses, and a forecast that conflates them tells neither story.

columns.name: track
columns.note: Which motion this goal measures. New business and renewals are tracked as separate lines under the same owner because the work is not comparable — a renewal at 90% and a new deal at 90% require completely different effort. 'Total' exists only for an overall number that genuinely rolls both up, and should never be the only goal.

columns.name: period_label
columns.note: FY27, Q3-FY27, Aug-2026. Must match how the org names periods.

columns.name: original_target
columns.note: What it was when first set. Kept so a moved goal is visible as a moved goal rather than quietly becoming the number that was always there.

columns.name: revision_reason
columns.note: Why it moved. Territory change, reforecast, headcount, market.

columns.name: currency
columns.note: ISO code this target is set in. A goal in the base currency needs no conversion and cannot drift with the rate.

columns.name: converted_currency
columns.note: DERIVED. Which currency converted_* is expressed in — the folder's base_currency at the moment of conversion. Stored per row rather than read from config, so a folder that later changes its base currency cannot silently reinterpret numbers already written.

columns.name: fx_rate
columns.note: DERIVED. The multiplier actually applied: amount x fx_rate = converted amount. Stored so the converted figure can be reconstructed and audited without guessing which rate was in force. 1 when the record is already in the base currency.

columns.name: fx_rate_date
columns.note: DERIVED. effective_from of the fx-rates row used. Not the same as when the conversion ran: a rate dated before the record's own date is the normal case, and a rate dated after it means no rate that old exists and fx.py --check will say so.

columns.name: fx_frozen
columns.note: DERIVED. yes once this record reaches a closed state, after which the converted figure is never recomputed — a closed number that moves with the exchange rate makes last quarter's attainment a different number every time it is read. Open records reconvert at the current rate on every run.

columns.name: converted_target
columns.note: DERIVED. The target in the base currency, from target x fx_rate. Blank — never zero — when target is blank, when currency is blank, or when no rate exists for that currency. A missing conversion that reads as zero silently shrinks a forecast.

columns.name: attained
columns.note: DERIVED from closed-won in period, summed in the BASE currency using each deal's converted amount. Compare it against converted_target, not target — target is in this goal's own currency and the two are only the same number for base-currency goals.

columns.name: attainment_pct
columns.note: DERIVED: attained / converted_target, both in the base currency.

columns.name: pace_required
columns.note: DERIVED: what still needs to close per remaining week to make it, in the base currency.

columns.name: on_track
columns.note: DERIVED against elapsed time, not just raw attainment — 40% at the half is on track, 40% at three-quarters is not

columns.name: last_confirmed
columns.note: When the user last confirmed this is still the number. Goals drift; an unconfirmed goal quietly makes every forecast wrong.

columns.name: confirm_cadence
columns.note: Default Quarterly. The forecast skill re-asks when last_confirmed is older than this.

columns.name: status
columns.note: Superseded rather than deleted when a goal is replaced — mid-year changes are part of the story

fx.note: A goal set in a currency other than the base one does move during its period as the rate moves, which is uncomfortable for a quota — the cure is to set the goal in the base currency, not to freeze a live target at a stale rate. It stops moving when the period ends or the goal is superseded. attained and attainment_pct are computed in the base currency and therefore compare against converted_target, not target.
